propositions.text: The service exposes a single evaluation call evaluate(flag_key, user) returning a boolean on/off decision for that user and flag at call time.
The user context carries at least a stable user_id string plus an arbitrary attribute bag consulted by targeting rules.
Evaluation is a pure deterministic function of current flag configuration and user context: same config plus same user always yields the same decision.
Inputs are applied in the fixed order kill switch, then targeting rules, then percentage rollout, then default, and this order determines conflict resolution.
An engaged global kill switch is checked first and forces the flag off for every user, overriding all targeting rules and the rollout.
Targeting rules are evaluated in listed order before the rollout, and the first matching rule decides the result immediately, short-circuiting the rollout.
If no rule matches and the rollout does not enable the user, the flag's configured default value is returned.
The percentage rollout is sticky per user id: a given user stays in the same bucket for a flag across calls, processes, and machines while the percentage is unchanged.
Bucket assignment is computed by hashing flag_key combined with user_id into 0..99, enabling the user iff the bucket is strictly less than the percentage, with no per-user state stored.
The percentage is an integer 0..100 inclusive, where 0 enables no users and 100 enables every user.
Every flag configuration change is recorded in an append-only audit log capturing who, when, the flag key, and before/after values, off the hot evaluation path so it never blocks evaluate.
Evaluation must not block on a network round trip and reads flag config from an in-memory snapshot rather than querying per call.
